purpose: Development cases for bounded research value evaluation; grader truth is stored separately.

cases.question: How many subsets of {1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8} have sum 9? Give one such subset and explain why the count is exhaustive.
expected_obligations: Give the exact number of subsets.
Give one subset with sum 9.
Explain why the enumeration covers every subset exactly once.

cases.question: For real x where the expression is defined, simplify (x^2 - 4)/(x - 2). State its domain and whether the simplified expression is equivalent at every real number.
expected_obligations: Give the simplified expression.
State the original domain.
Explain the excluded input and distinguish equality on the domain from equality of domains.

cases.question: Is n^2+n+41 prime for every nonnegative integer n? Determine the truth of the statement and support your conclusion.
expected_obligations: Give a correct truth value.
If false, provide and verify a counterexample.
Keep any finite testing claim within the range actually checked.
forbidden_claims: Claiming finite checks prove a universal statement.

cases.question: What meeting time is supported by these records? Distinguish the original schedule from the current instruction and explain the basis.

sources.text: Draft schedule v1, created Monday: project review, Thursday at 09:30 local time.
Signed amendment v2, created Tuesday by the organizer: project review moved to Thursday at 10:00 local time. This amendment replaces the time in v1.

expected_obligations: Report the current meeting time.
Identify the earlier time as superseded.
Attribute the current time to the signed amendment.
forbidden_claims: Treating both records as equally current.

cases.question: A proof claims that sqrt(2) is rational: write sqrt(2)=a/b in lowest terms, square to get a^2=2b^2, and conclude that a and b are both even. Is the proof valid? Assess the conclusion and justify your answer.
expected_obligations: Give a correct conclusion about the proof and claim.
Explain what follows from a^2=2b^2.
Identify the contradiction with lowest terms.
forbidden_claims: Accepting the claim that sqrt(2) is rational.
Claiming both-even contradicts lowest terms without explaining why.

cases.question: How many usable units remain, and how many were originally shipped? Show how the records combine and state any limitation.

sources.text: Packing specification for this shipment: each carton contains 8 units.
Receiving record: 3 units were damaged in transit and are not usable.

expected_obligations: Compute original shipped units.
Compute usable units.
Show the arithmetic and identify the records used.
forbidden_claims: Inferring facts outside the supplied records.

cases.question: Prove that for every positive integer n, 1 + 3 + 5 + ... + (2n - 1) = n^2. Give a concise proof.
expected_obligations: State the identity for all positive integers n.
Give a valid proof, such as induction or a direct pairing argument.
forbidden_claims: Checking only finitely many values as proof of the universal identity.
